run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-101 had issues on November 20, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: The exact entity named, a payment-api pod in namespace app-101, is not returned by the Kubernetes pod view; namespace app-101 at 2026-11-21T04:48Z held only the loki pod and Deployment loki. Loki does hold payment-api application logs for namespace app-101 under pod label payment-api-101-8486559b69-lgn6x / service payment-api, and those logs show the incident: eight ERROR lines 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' between 2026-11-20T13:46:00Z and 14:44:00Z, with wait_time_ms 1227-4840 and queue_length 5-15, starting four minutes after an INFO 'Payment processed successfully' at 13:42 and followed by INFO successes from 14:49 onward. Within the returned rows the process logged no restart during the burst; the only 'Payment API started' line is at 2026-11-21T04:47:03Z. So the observed event is database connection-pool exhaustion inside payment-api, not a crash. Why the pool was exhausted is unresolved: no database object or logs are observable, and every Prometheus and Jaeger query failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so request rate, error rate, latency and DB-side signals could not be checked. Conclusion is partial; no single root-cause object can be named from the available evidence.

claims.text: The Kubernetes pod view for namespace app-101 returned exactly one pod, loki-66445c6d6f-d22xx (Running, 0 restarts, owner ReplicaSet loki-66445c6d6f); no pod named payment-api* was present at 2026-11-21T04:48:41Z, and the app-101 Deployment view likewise returned only Deployment loki with 1/1 ready replicas.

Loki does contain payment-api logs for a related-but-different identity: streams labeled namespace=app-101, job=payment-api, service=payment-api, file /var/log/payment-api.log, pod=payment-api-101-8486559b69-lgn6x.

Eight ERROR lines from pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-lgn6x, all reading 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted', occur between 2026-11-20T13:46:00Z and 2026-11-20T14:44:00Z; each carries wait_time_ms (1227, 2104, 1495, 2965, 4005, 4840, 2358, 3836) and queue_length (10, 11, 8, 9, 10, 8, 15, 5).

The pool-exhausted burst begins at 13:46:00Z, four minutes after an INFO line 'Payment processed successfully' (payment_id PAY-5032) at 2026-11-20T13:42:00Z; a query restricted to 13:35-13:50 returned only those two lines, so the first observed failure is the 13:46 ERROR.

In the 36 rows returned for the whole authorized window for {namespace="app-101"}, the newest ERROR is the 14:44:00Z line and every later row is INFO: 'Payment processed successfully' at 14:49, 15:27, 17:01, 17:38, 19:25, 21:47, 21:52, 22:19, 00:30, 00:34, 01:12, 01:39, 03:15, 03:54, plus 'Payment API started' (port 8080) at 2026-11-21T04:47:03.761224Z.

No restart or startup line appears in the returned logs between 13:42Z and 14:49Z on 2026-11-20; the only 'Payment API started' event in the window is at 2026-11-21T04:47:03Z, so the 13:46-14:44Z failure occurred in a continuously running process rather than across a crash/restart.

A log-count metric query over 2026-11-20T09:00-15:00Z grouped by namespace/job/level returned only two series, both job=payment-api namespace=app-101: level=ERROR count 8 and level=INFO count 7; no other job or service logs are present in Loki for that period.

Namespace app-101 also has a Deployment payment-api-101 whose ReplicaSet payment-api-101-8486559b69 was scaled from 0 to 1 at 2026-11-21T04:47:02Z, creating pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-lgn6x (containers payment-api and promtail started 04:47:03-04:47:04Z), and the same pod's containers were stopped at 2026-11-21T04:47:15Z; neither the Deployment nor the ReplicaSet is listed now and the pod is absent from the current pod list.

The app-101 log pipeline is a file scrape run by promtail: ConfigMap promtail-config defines job_name payment-api with labels job=payment-api, namespace=app-101, __path__=/var/log/*.log, and a pipeline that parses the JSON fields timestamp/level/message/service/pod and uses the line's own RFC3339 timestamp, so entry times come from the application payload rather than ingestion time.

The cluster objects visible now postdate the incident: every otel-demo pod (including payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d) was created 2026-11-20T16:32-16:33Z and app-101's loki/promtail harness objects at 2026-11-21T04:46-04:47Z, so incident-time pod status for 13:45Z on 2026-11-20 cannot be reconstructed from current objects.

Deployment payment in namespace otel-demo - a different entity from app-101 payment-api - has a single ReplicaSet payment-6f7bc865d6 at deployment revision 1 with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment, i.e. no pod-template rollout occurred there.

otel-demo pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d (different entity) shows restartCount 1 with last termination reason Unknown, exitCode 255, finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z, and its 03:48-04:48Z logs on 2026-11-21 are routine 'Charge request received.' INFO lines plus one MetadataLookupWarning about an invalid Metadata-Flavor header.

The flagd-config ConfigMap in otel-demo lists payment-related fault flags with defaultVariant "off" (paymentFailure variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off, paymentUnreachable on/off) alongside productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adFailure, cartFailure, kafkaQueueProblems and imageSlowLoad, all default "off"; this flag set governs otel-demo services, not the app-101 payment-api.

The payment-api's database dependency was slow or saturated during 13:46-14:44Z, so requests waited and the fixed-size connection pool ran dry (observed waits of 1.2-4.8 s and queue depth 5-15); the database side itself is unverified because no database object, log stream or metric was observable.

Alternatively the payment-api connection pool's own capacity or settings (for example a reduced pool size or shorter acquisition timeout applied shortly before 13:46Z) produced the exhaustion; change history is not integrated in this Run and app-101 holds no payment-api ConfigMap, so this remains unverified.

A load increase on payment-api could also have driven the pool exhaustion, but no request-rate, concurrency or error-rate series could be read for payment-api because every Prometheus query in this Run failed, so this cannot be confirmed or excluded.

Rejected: that the app-101 payment-api pod crashed, was OOM-killed or crash-looped during the incident. The returned log rows show no restart/startup between 13:42Z and 14:49Z, the only 'Payment API started' row is at 2026-11-21T04:47:03Z, and the failure text itself is about acquiring a database connection, not about process termination.

Rejected: that the otel-demo payment deployment/pod restart or its flagd paymentFailure/paymentUnreachable flags caused this event. That is a different entity (namespace otel-demo, pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d, Deployment payment revision 1), its restart at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z is roughly 14 hours after the app-101 error burst, every otel-demo pod restarted at the same moment, and both payment flags read defaultVariant "off" in the current ConfigMap.

Rejected: that the app-101 changes inside the window (Deployment loki scaled 0->1 at 2026-11-21T04:46:39Z with ReplicaSet loki-66445c6d6f SuccessfulCreate, and pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-lgn6x created 04:47:02Z with containers stopped 04:47:15Z) were impact of the 13:46Z failure. They are controller-driven create/delete events of the log-collection harness, occur over 14 hours after the burst, and are Normal events, not failures of the workload under investigation.

Restore or re-point the Prometheus/Jaeger read path (the prometheus-readonly-proxy route), then check payment-api request rate, error ratio and latency around 13:46-14:44Z and any DB-side saturation metrics, to test the load-versus-dependency hypotheses.

Identify the database that payment-api connects to and review its connection limits and payment-api's pool configuration (max pool size, acquisition timeout), since the observed symptom is pool exhaustion with 1.2-4.8 s wait times and queue depth up to 15; consult change history (not integrated here) for changes applied shortly before 13:46Z.

gaps: Every Prometheus tool call in this Run failed: metrics_range_query (multiple windows/queries), execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_all_labels, list_prometheus_rules and get_prometheus_target all returned status error/SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE between 04:48:52Z and 04:50:47Z, so no metric evidence exists for payment-api request rate, error rate, latency, resource saturation or any database metric.

Every Jaeger tool call (traces_search, traces_list_services, traces_list_operations) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no trace evidence exists for the app-101 payment-api, although pod jaeger-698d849b7b-sjz9c itself is Running/ready and logged 'Query server started' at 2026-11-21T04:23:48Z.
change_history is listed as not integrated, so no evidence about configuration/pool-size/traffic changes near 13:45Z on 2026-11-20 could be obtained.

The database dependency is unidentified and unobservable: a Loki query for jobs postgres|mysql|db|database|redis|payment-db in namespace app-101 over 12:00-15:00Z returned no_data, and no database pod, service, endpoint or ConfigMap exists among the cluster objects read.

No Kubernetes events exist for the incident period: the events view returned only events between 2026-11-21T04:23:43Z and 2026-11-21T04:47:15Z, so nothing is known from events about 2026-11-20T13:45Z.

Incident-time pod state for the app-101 payment-api cannot be read: pod payment-api-101-8486559b69-lgn6x no longer exists, so its status, restart count, last termination reason and container exit code at 13:46Z are unknown, and the exact-name entity 'payment-api pod in namespace app-101' returned nothing in the pod and deployment views.

Loki data for app-101 is a sampled/backfilled promtail file scrape of /var/log/payment-api.log (36 rows returned for the whole 24h window; the 13:35-13:50 window returned only 2 rows), so log-line counts must not be read as request counts or as a complete error rate.

A Loki query for {namespace="app-101"} returned no data in 2026-11-21T04:30-04:48Z, and a query for {namespace="app-101", level="ERROR"} after 2026-11-20T14:45Z returned no_data; these empty results show only that those queries matched nothing and are not proof that no error occurred after 14:44Z.

No NetworkPolicy objects exist in the cluster (networkpolicies query returned no_data), so NetworkPolicy blocking cannot be confirmed as either a cause or a ruled-out factor for any refused connection.

It cannot be determined whether the connection pool was exhausted by a slow/saturated database, by a reduced pool configuration, or by increased request load, because no metric, trace, change-history or database-side evidence was obtainable.
next_steps: Repair or re-authorize the Prometheus read path and query traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"} / rpc and http duration series and any DB client pool metrics for 2026-11-20 13:00-15:00Z.
Establish the database identity used by payment-api and inspect its connection limits, pgbouncer/pooler settings and slow-query logs for 13:46-14:44Z on 2026-11-20.

Review the payment-api connection-pool configuration (max connections, acquisition timeout, queue limit) and its deployment manifest as it stood on 2026-11-20, plus any change record near 13:45Z, since change history is not integrated in this Run.
Check whether request volume to payment-api rose before 13:46Z (load-generator or ingress request-rate series) once metrics access is restored.
